meta.title: Lydian in a Window You Already Own
meta.summary: A Lydian's CAGED windows are A major's CAGED windows with the 4 raised a fret, and because a window's edges are fixed frets, that raise pushes dots across the frame in a direction you can predict.

spans.text: One degree separates Lydian from the major scale:
, and nothing else moves. Here's exactly what that single change does to a window you already know.
Same five windows, same places. A window is anchored on the root, not the scale —
The Window Stays, the Third Moves
already made that case for major against minor, and it holds here too. There's no Lydian shape to learn, only a degree to raise inside a window you already own.

The same window with the fourth raised — eighteen dots

spans.text: , one fret below the window's bottom edge, and raising it brought that copy into the frame. Seventeen dots become eighteen.

State the rule once, correctly: the window doesn't move. Raising a degree moves its dot up one fret, so a dot sitting on the top fret raises straight out of the picture, and a dot sitting just below the bottom edge raises into it. "The same picture with one dot moved" is false as a caption for what just happened — true of the notes, false of the diagram.
Nothing New to Learn on the Neck
already made this exact point for a different pair of scales. Fix the direction in your head: raising a degree only ever moves its dot toward the top edge of a window, never the bottom.
